analysis:
Examined all supplied scheduler excerpts and the bounded patch against the indexed threat model and detailed T-041 definition. The patch in MultiModelBatchSchedulerEngine.swift initializes media reasoning state from rendered prompt tokens (head 714–724) and passes that state into stop-string scope selection (head 747–749). This couples output classification and stopping behavior; the supplied additions do not establish an authorization, encryption, cache-isolation or billing regression. The local content-seed option is distinct from coordinator construction in the visible head source (57–60, 235–241, 298–303). Internal tool-schema metadata remains permitted for coordinator construction and rejected for local construction (204, 270, 459–462). Remote cache scope and native-local fallback remain separately represented (102–110, 442–443), relevant to T-041.
The BASE media path disables caching, carries the absolute deadline, and installs terminal-draining forwarding (1101–1113). Its forwarder preserves typed terminal usage, rejects missing media terminals, validates tool calls and releases ownership (1297–1428, 1453–1482); these are relevant to T-010, A-018 and billing integrity but cannot establish the changed HEAD behavior by themselves. No concrete regression is supported in this source slice. Integration must inspect the omitted changed HEAD regions at 975–976 and 1106–1108 and reconcile the moved media-prefix calculation with ReasoningPromptProbe, ReasoningStopScope and downstream channel parsing. Verify open/pre-closed prompt handling and cancellation/terminal usage remain consistent; the truncated removal hunk and absent changed HEAD source leave these conclusions unresolved. No unchanged external authorization or cryptographic implementation was examined.
